overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law on all three allegations: it entered executive session for an improper purpose (G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(7)) on four dates, gave insufficient notice of the topics, and the Chair's pre-session statements lacked detail. Ordered compliance, training, minutes release, and certification.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board entered executive session for an improper purpose at its March 17, March 24, April 7 and April 15, 2014 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by entering into executive session for an improper purpose on the four dates discussed above.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the meeting notices failed to give sufficient specificity about the executive session topics for the four meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Even if the Board had a valid reason to enter into executive session under Purpose 7, as the Board's Counsel has argued, it failed to properly notice the executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair's verbal statements before entering executive session at the four meetings lacked sufficient specificity about the purpose.
allegations.key_passage: the Chair failed to include sufficient detail in statements made prior to entering into executive session during those meetings.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation).
Board members to review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law training video on executive session.

Release to the public the portions of the executive session minutes pertaining to the retiree health premium discussions held March 17, March 24, April 7 and April 15, 2014, with no withholding or redaction.
Certify compliance in writing to the Division of Open Government, using the attached forms, within thirty days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Board that a similar, future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law.
